step_by_step_reasoning:
Step 1: Considered knowledge-base functions — there are none available in the provided environment, so none were applicable or used.

Step 2 (Locate product): The product grid is showing many pages. The filter inputs in the grid are accessible as unlabeled textboxes. Based on the accessibility tree, the Name filter textbox appears to be the fifth textbox in document order (index 4, 0-based). I first attempt to fill page.get_by_role("textbox").nth(4) with the product name. If that fails, I fall back to the group-level Search textbox or the first textbox on the page.

Step 3 (Apply filter): I click the Search button inside the cell named "Reset Filter Search" using the full get_by_role path to avoid ambiguity. If that path isn't available I fall back to a top-level Search button.

Step 4 (Open product): After the grid refresh, I iterate over all rows and compare each row's inner_text to find the one containing the product name. When found, I click the scoped Edit link inside that row (rows.nth(i).get_by_role("link", name="Edit")). If the Edit link isn't labeled exactly, I fall back to clicking the first link inside the row.

Step 5 (Open Custom Options): On the product edit page I try to open the Custom Options section by trying role types in order: tab, link, button, using page.get_by_role(role, name="Custom Options").click()

Step 6 (Add new option): I try common labels for the add-control ("Add New Option", "Add Option", etc.), and if none match, I search for any button containing the text 'Add' and click it. I scope button clicks with get_by_role when possible to be precise.

Step 7 (Configure option): To set the option title I search for textboxes named "Title" and fill the last one with "Size" (new option typically appears at the end). To choose the option type I search for comboboxes named "Type" and select the last one with label "Drop-down". If those named controls are not present, I fallback to filling the last textbox/first combobox available.

Step 8 (Add value): I then attempt to add the option value "XXXL" by filling a suitable Title textbox — if multiple Title textboxes exist I fill the last one; otherwise I try one of the last few textboxes on the page.

Step 9 (Save): I click the Save button as the final action to persist the change; if that button isn't available I try "Save and Continue Edit" and then any button whose name matches /Save/i as a last resort. The Save click is last because it may navigate away from the page.

Notes on selector strategy: I used scoped get_by_role calls when interacting with elements that belong to a larger parent (for example, clicking Search inside the Reset Filter Search cell and clicking Edit inside a matched row). This follows the instruction to use full get_by_role paths to avoid ambiguity. I also included small waits (wait_for_load_state and asyncio.sleep) to allow Magento's dynamic UI to render.

If any critical step fails (product not found, cannot open Custom Options), the script raises an exception so the caller can detect the failure. The code does not change language settings and keeps everything in English.
